property_summary: The reference contract never sends its entire balance when block.number % 15 != 0, but the buggy contract only sends when block.number % 15 != 0, so it will send balance on a non-multiple-of-15 block if the other conditions are met.

For any sequence of admissible fallback calls, the reference contract ensures pastBlockTime strictly increases after each call, while the buggy version allows it to remain unchanged or not increase when a second call occurs in the same block with the same timestamp.

For any two admissible fallback() calls to C, the reference contract guarantees that after both calls complete, pastBlockTime equals the timestamp of the second call, while the buggy version allows pastBlockTime to equal the timestamp of the first call when both calls occur in the same block.

After two admissible fallback calls in the same block, the reference contract's pastBlockTime always equals block.timestamp of the second call, while the buggy version can leave it equal to the first call's timestamp.
After every fallback call, the contract's ether balance is zero if and only if the call value was exactly 10 ether; the bug allows non-10 ether calls to also trigger the same balance-draining logic.

The original contract's ether balance is always zero after any successful fallback call, but the buggy mutant can accumulate balance when calls with non‑10 ether are made and block.number is not divisible by 15, leaving the balance non‑zero.

For any sequence of calls with various msg.value, after each call that succeeds, the contract's balance is always 0 if the call value was 10 ether; the mutant allows a non-10 ether call when block.number % 15 != 0 to succeed and leave a non-zero balance, breaking the invariant that a successful fallback always drains all funds when 10 ether is sent and never drains them otherwise.

After any admissible call to fallback(), the contract's total ether balance must be zero whenever the caller would have received it in the reference version; the bug violates this by never sending the balance, leaving it > 0.
After any admissible call to fallback(), if the call did not revert, the contract's balance is zero when block.number % 15 == 0; the bug violates this by never sending the balance, leaving it > 0.
